description_text:
This is my rendition of a 2 Stroke Radio Controlled Gas Engine.  As a Radio Control enthusiast, I commonly use 50 and 100 cc gas engines in my larger wooden and composite aircraft.  Now I present a model that will give you an accurate representation of either a single or twin cylinder small gas engine. 
The model is native to Cinema 4D R15 and is subdivision ready made almost entirely of quads.  For other programs I have enabled a defaulted subdivision factor of 2.  Lower or higher resolution models available upon request.  In this collection you will receive both my single and twin cylinder gas engine.  Don't like it's layout, makes some adjustments and you can turn it into the engine you want.  Purposely built so the cylinder can rotate however desired along with the exhaust cans.
If you are trying to show off an RC model or need a small 2 stroke gas engine, this is the model for you at a low price.  Many hours of work has gone into this model, it is an exterior detailed model only no internal components.   Most all the components use materials (if you are using a program aside from C4D, use your favorite metal materials to make this model shine).  Only one texture is used for the spark plug line.
NOTE: This model is native to Cinema 4D, all renders were created using C4D R15 and may not reflect other programs in terms of materials. Polygons represent the low resolution C4D model (Available for other programs on request).
If this model meets or exceeds your expectations please comment and like. Happy Modelling!
If you like this model check out my others under jasoncrohr.

title: Plummer block pedestal bearing Free 3D model

description_text:
Plummer block or Pedestal bearing is used for long shafts, requiring intermediate support, especially when the shaft
cannot be introduced in the bearing end-wise. It consists of a pedestal or base, a cap and a
bush, split into two halves, called ‘bearing brasses’. The split parts used in the assembly, facilitate
easy assembly and periodical replacement of the worn-out brasses.
After placing the journal on the lower half of the bush, kept in the base, the upper half
of the bush is placed and the cap is then fixed to the pedestal, by means of two bolts.
Flanges are provided at either end of the bush, to prevent its axial motion. The rotary motion
of the bush is prevented by a snug provided at the bottom of the lower brass, fitting into a
corresponding hole in the base.

GE CP 0

In my experience that is now working in public street lighting company, I've made a sealing for our company and it's products successfully in a test dive in the sea reaches a depth of about 36 meters (but ultimately plastic ABS which we use as the main material of body cracks) that are not could be deeper at that time.
I use a seal with a simple profile with screw locking method (because our products are round), so that the method inspired me in making this current design.
To produce a good sealing, the seal needs to be pressed with a precise and powerful, and I think snapfit method less suitable, so I decided to use the M3 countersink screws for locking.
Description:
QUICK CONNECTOR & QUICK CONNECTOR CORNER

  - Using the method Die Casting (Aluminum) for the mass production process.

  - Formation of simple geometry and is very easy to do with the process of Die Casting.

  - Processed tapping M3 for locking.

  - Lightweight but strong.

  - To finish coated with anti-rust sort of fluid that is not easy to rust.

This component serves to suppress and position the Brick. Brick will hit the seal underneath.
I positioned this component not only on cut but also amid to generate pressure on the SEAL balanced. Reduce the possibility of leaks in the middle of construction.
BRICK
No changes to these components (as default)
SEAL

  - Using the method RUBBER INJECTION MOLD the material NBR.

  - Formation of simple geometry, only 5mm diameter circular profile.

  - Easily mounted to the component Brick.

  - I do not loose the BRICK so it can be terrifying BRICK to produce a better sealing.

CAVITY

  - Created by injection mold process.

  - Just as the default specification.

  - Just added profile to cradle the head bolt M3 Counter Sink, so the existing molding live repaired to add this profile

GE CP 0
Easily installed and removed , and a width of not more than 49 + 1 mm .
Construction of components installed neatly , no component is annoying when used to lower the risk of Quick Connector nudged when used .

description_text:
This is a stand-alone filament spool holder with gearwheel bearings. All parts including the bearing can be 3D printed.
Assembly Steps
Step 1: 3D print the following parts:4 x bearings --> this should be a good quality print with at least 50% infill.2 x body2 x shaft --> You might want to scale this along the long axis if you find the holder too big. The length of the shaft will determine the maximum width of spools that can be used.
Step 2: Loosen the gear wheels using some force and if needed a head screwdriver. Then I used an electric screwdriver to turn each bearing for about 1-2 minutes and afterwards I applied WD40 so they run smoothly.
Step 3: Put everything together like on the pictures. Then you will need some glue to hold everything in place. Don't glue the bearings to the shaft, they need to be able to slide to allow usage of spools with different width. For this step I used cyanoacrylatic glue.
Thanks to Ross Korsky and his Fusion Add-On for helical gears: https://apps.autodesk.com/FUSION/en/Detail/Index?id=9029586664984391977&appLang=en&os=Win64

The Shuriken of Omens is based on the Sword of Omens, a powerful and iconic weapon featured in the Thundercats animated series (original and reboot). The sword has been recreated many times, so I tried to redesign the sword, creating a new iconic weapon. The shuriken is designed for easy printing and assembly. The top and bottom caps hold it together, but also feature the 2 states of the Eye of Thundera (closed/Cat's eye).   A stand, featuring the cat's eye is also included for the shuriken.
The shuriken includes the original and version 2. V2 is provided as a zipped file, including updated topology, new display stand options, and a revised clasp core to hold the body together. 
Some parts have elevated sections, which can't be printed directly on the print bed. In such cases, supports are necessary. For the cleanest results, for parts needing them, I used supports with the support roof enabled @ 100% density. If property calibrated, you should be able to peal or pop part right off, with fewer artifacts. Also, it easier separate from the roof than from direct supports.  In this case, the distance between model and roof was a bit too high, but something like 0.1 or 0.15 seems to work quite well. My One Piece shuriken turned out even better.
The blades of the shuriken can fold. Assemble with blades folded to achieve proper alignment and easier assemble. 
Required Parts2 collar3 blades1 top cap (open eye)1 top body (front)1 bottom body (back)1 bottom cap (closed eye)1 gear1 stand (optional)
Suggested assembly method...
  - Thread the bottom cap through the top body.

  - Slide the gear over the threaded end of the cap.

  - With each in folded position, slide blades over the pivots of the top body.

  - Place the bottom body over the gear, blades, and threaded cap.

  - Thread the remaining cap through the bottom body and screw into the bottom cap.(Not so tight that it fractures the cap; nor so tight that it interferes with blade movement)

For vesrion 2, twist the connected eye counter clockwise to lock parts in place.

description_text:
16-tooth spur gear, accurately modeled and ready for use in CAD, CGI, and 3D print applications. Modeled in Autodesk Inventor and Carrara Studio and provided in multiple file formats (STP, SAT, IGS, OBJ, FBX, 3DS, CAR, and STL). Perfect for both digital and physical mechanical design projects.
Gear tooth profile is precisely modeled with accurate involute geometry and a small amount of backlash to ensure proper engagement. Pressure angle is a standard 14.5 degrees. Diametrical pitch is provided as 16 teeth/inch. Gear can be easily scaled to create any diametrical pitch or module that you may need.
Gear is provided in 3 styles:

  - Drive - gear includes hub and bore that locks to standard ANSI D-profile shaft, optional set screw is included

  - Idle - gear includes hub and bore that spins freely around standard round-profile shaft

  - Template - gear has no hub and includes pilot hole that can be remodeled or drilled to any size that you may need

Each gear style is provided in 8 file formats:

  - STP (general solid model format for CAD)

  - SAT (general solid model format for CAD)

  - IGS (general solid model format for CAD)

  - OBJ with external materials (general surface model format for CGI)

  - FBX (general surface model format for CGI)

  - 3DS (general surface model format for CGI)

  - CAR (Carrara Studio format for CGI)

  - STL (general surface model format for 3D print)

Want more gears that are compatible with this product? Download the complete 127-piece collection: https://www.cgtrader.com/3d-print-models/hobby-diy/mechanical-parts/modular-gear-collection-01

Gear specifications:
  - 16-Tooth, round bore with keyway (1.00in pitch diameter, 25.4mm reference diameter)
Gear tooth profile is precisely modeled with accurate arc-based geometry and a small amount of backlash to ensure proper engagement. Gear can be used as drive gear (rotationally locked to shaft) or idle gear (free spinning about shaft).
Gear is provided with a diametrical pitch of 16 teeth/inch (module 1.6). Gear bore is designed for a 0.25in (6.35mm) nominal shaft size. Gear has a 0.25in (6.35mm) face width. Gear can be easily scaled to create any diametrical pitch or module that you may need.
The centerline distance between any two mating gears is ( First Gear Pitch Diameter + Second Gear Pitch Diameter ) / 2.
Gear is provided in 8 file formats:

  - STP (general solid model format for CAD)

  - SAT (general solid model format for CAD)

  - IGS (general solid model format for CAD)

  - OBJ (general surface model format for CGI)

  - FBX (general surface model format for CGI)

  - 3DS (general surface model format for CGI)

  - CAR (Carrara Studio format for CGI))

  - STL (general surface model format for 3D print)

Product also includes 2 drawings (DWG and PDF formats) and a Read Me text file (TXT format) detailing the physical dimensions of the gear.

description_text:
80 mm 3jaw chuck A chuck is a specialized type of clamp used to hold an object with radial symmetry, especially a cylinder. In drills and mills it holds the rotating tool whereas in lathes it holds the rotating workpiece. On a lathe the chuck is mounted on the spindle which rotates within the headstock. For some purposes (such as drilling) an additional chuck may be mounted on the non-rotating tailstock.
Many chucks have jaws, (sometimes called dogs) that are arranged in a radially symmetrical pattern like the points of a star. The jaws are tightened up to hold the tool or workpiece. Often the jaws will be tightened or loosened with the help of a chuck key, which is a wrench-like tool made for the purpose.[citation needed] Many jawed chucks, however, are of the keyless variety, and their tightening and loosening is by hand force alone. Keyless designs offer the convenience of quicker and easier chucking and unchucking, but have a lower gripping force to hold the tool or workpiece, which is potentially more of a problem with cylindrical than hexagonal shanks. Collet chucks, rather than having jaws, have collets, which are flexible collars or sleeves that fit closely around the tool or workpiece and grip it when squeezed.
Chucks on some lathes have jaws that move independently, allowing them to hold irregularly shaped objects. A few chuck designs are even more complex, involving specially shaped jaws, higher numbers of jaws, quick-release mechanisms, or other special features.
Magnetic and vacuum chucks are also made, with typically flat surfaces against which workpieces or tools are firmly held by the pressure of their respective force.
To chuck a tool or workpiece is to hold it with a chuck, in which case it has been chucked. Chucking individual slugs or blanks on a lathe is often called chucking work. In bar work or bar feed work the stock protrudes from the chuck, is worked upon, then parted off (cut off) rather than sawn. Automatic lathes that specialize in chucking work are often called chuckers.

description_text:
Summary:
Contains four replacement elements for Ender 6:
Z-axis bracket: maintains Z-axis vibrationless
Extruder housing: lightweight replacement to make gantry lighter and reduce ringing
X-axis spring-squeeze roller plate: reduces wear on rollers, less damping on stepper motion.20mm long conical M5 screws and original rollers used.
Y-axis spring-squeeze roller plates (print two).20mm long conical M5 screws and original rollers used.
Overall, replacement reduces gantry weight by about 170 gram.
Post printing:
Clean the main contact surfaces with a file, removing any loose/hanging threading
Roller plates have no threading printed, use M5 thread cutter for a fine, precise threading.
Note that gantry may not be precisely mounted from factory, spacing material between plates and the U-pieces might be needed, or full detachment and realignment of parts, which is a riskier proposition.
For the X-axis plate, the two CoreXY band ends are a bit in the way and should be pulled back with two small zip ties. To mount the part into the big holes, use two lock nuts with the plastic ground out with a thread cutter, and screw them on REVERSED. The lock nuts will snugly fit into the two holes.
Two washers go into the Y-axis plates to offload screw stress onto the plates, do not mount without them.Use 6mm diameter springs.
For the Z-axis bracket: it will fit into the two existing holes on the back, use 20mm long flathead screws.

formats_detail: [{"format": "STL", "full_name": "Stereolithography", "file_size": "90 KB", "file_count": 1, "version": "1.0", "renderer": null}]
cgt_checks_passed: geometry.nonManifoldVertices, geometry.openEdges, geometry.noBadContiguousEdges, geometry.noNgons, geometry.noSelfIntersections, geometry.nonManifoldFaces, geometry.overlappingFaces, geometry.zeroLengthEdge, geometry.zeroFaceArea, scene.centeredGeometryBoundingBox
description_text:
Circular linkage with no fixed center.This particular mechanism can be expanded and contracted as it shows in the video demonstration.It is a model that can be easily printed on all 3D printers.
Print settings (PLA):

  - For all the files use 2mm layer and no supports. 100% infill recommended.

  - The stl files Circular_link_lock and Circular_link_pin may be printed at low speeds (around 20mm/s) to make sure that them don't unstick from the hotbed during printing time. It's also recommended to enable the option Z hop when retracted (betwen 0.4 and 1mm) to make sure that the hot end don't rubs the print and unstick it (because those two files dont't have much contact area to the hot bed.
-The stl file Circular_link_arm can be printed at higher speeds (up to 50mm/s).

Assembly:
-You'll need x24Circular_link_arm, x36 Circular_link_pin and x36 Circular_link_lock. (Circular_link_lock is not necessary to print, but is a safe way to make sure that the mechanism stays in place and don't get loose.
To assembly the mechanism is really simple. Take x2 Circular_link_arm . Just make sure that the flat parts (in contact with the hot bed) are facing out. Join them as shown in the fifth picture using x1Circular_link_pin".
To fit the pin into the arm, you need to bend the pin as sown in the seventh and eighth pictures. It makes the pin to fit in the holes of the arms. Later you have to insert a 2mm allen key or similar into the pin as shown in ninth and tenth pictures to prevent the pins to fall off. You may also put one Circular_link_lock in each side of the pin to lock the pins in place.
I recommend to make x12 units made by x2 arms, x1 pin and x2 locks (in cross shape, like the ninth picture).Join the x12 units toegether to make the Circular linkage.

description_text:
This one part Bird feeder is designed for small birds. You can leave some food for them here :-) .
It is super easy to make. It is just one print that takes around 5 hours to print and uses around 50 gram of filament. I added a screen shot of Cura where you can see the print settings. That gives you an idea where the 50 grams of filament come from.
I tested this model with a 0.4mm Nozzle, without Print Support material. It is important to set the cooling of the print at maximum, when the 3d Printer reaches the top. Otherwise the ring(eye) on the top may deform a bit. It happened in my case and you can see it on the Photos as an example.At 100% size this Bird Feeder is 156mm high and has a diameter of +/- 76mm.
If you have any questions, feel free to ask :-)

description_text:
This is a very simple but usefull tool box. You can have all your spare parts aranged in one single space on the side of your printer without any intromission with your working area. It is designed to be attached to the left rail of your printer. You just have to unscrew the three bolts of the mother board box and gently slize the four bases. It has round holes on the bottom to attach a couple of 6mm x 1mm round magnets. But you can attach it with hot glue or similar.
It has been designed in sketchup and converted in several formats just in case you want to edit it.
I´m adding an stl format that was saved with the requirements to print on an Ender 3
I´m adding also a gcode format that is ready to print on an Ender 3 series.
The presets are in LOW QUALITY. I experienced a very good printing with this settings, but if you want a better finish I sugest you to print it in super quality or dinamic quality. There are no support nor plate adhesion.
Temperature was set for PLA at 195° on the nozzle and 50° on the printing bed. This settings are the best for my printer.

description_text:
UPDATED DESIGN by https://www.printableconcrete.com/ : Use the masking ring to easily glue the hook and form a beautiful joint. The rope organizer hook secures your coils of rope in your cockpit. Use 3mm thick bungee cord to hold the coils up and secure to the hook. The knot is neatly hidden from sight in the dedicated knot chamber. The foot provides a large area to glue the hook to a flat section of your cockpit wall. No drilling is needed, so there is no risk of leaks. Secure the masking tool to the cockpit surface using masking tape. Use a thick layer of sika or other similar glue between the back side of the hook and the cockpit surface. At the end of life cycle just cut the glue layer with an exacto knife and remove the glue residues. A yellowish mark on the gel coat might be visible after removal, but that will whiten out with time and UV exposure.
Printing
Use PLA as it is compatible with most glues and is plenty strong for this application. 2-3 perimeters and around 30-60 percent triangular infill works great. The steepest overhang is 65 degrees, so it is best to chose a low layer height or set it to variable.

This is the 13th piece to print and build the giant 1/72nd RMS Titanic model. You will need to purchase and print all other files to complete the project as you go.
You will require a 3d printer with a minimum build volume of 300mm wide, 300mm deep, and 400mm tall.

If your download on CGTrader does not work (CGTrader problem with free models):https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Cs3RVnAJXVN2GNslU-_rHyk-QtuGCFWe?usp=drive_link
Join the official M-Jet facebook group! https://www.facebook.com/groups/623045356071128
This is the new version of my 50cm jetsprint hull. You get all files I used to build my hull. It can be made using fibreglass or carbon fiber.
The hull will work very well with the M-Jet 30 or M-Jet 35.Full build playlist:https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLiFskGz_svvQw7cqP4VM8fh8YDrXtK8r6
Update 16.8.2022: Template for cutting the flood chamber hole was added to the Hull folder.
Update 18.11.2022: STEP files for the cover lid assembly were added to the Cover lid folder.
Update 19.11.2022: File for the rear wing was missing, now it was added into the Rear_wing folder.
Update 28.12.2022: A DXF file for cutting the cover lid hull cut was added into the Hull folder.
Update 4.1.2023: Two DXF files for cutting the flood chamber wall, and the rear flood chamber hole were added into the Hull folder. Please keep in mind that even after accurate CNC cut, the flood chamber wall will need a lot of sanding and tweaking to fit the inaccurate inner hull shape properly. Also, STL and STEP files for a pipe bender to bend the rollcage were added into the Rollcage folder. 
Update 4.7.2023: A STEP file for the whole 4G hull, as well as a simplified STEP file of the hull shape, were added to the files. 
Update 25.8.2023: A new MODS_for_4G_Sprint_Hull folder was added. It contains a bottom mould file with the spray rails included in the mould. This might make the moulding process more difficult, but does not require glueing the spray rails on later.
Update 11.10.2023: All folders were moved into one zip file to reduce the amount of CGTrader download errors. This is due to the model being free, there is a weird free download limit which I unfortunately cannot do anything about.
Update 19.10.2023: New softer versions of the TPU lid with thinner walls for more flexibility and easier operation were added into the Cover Lid folder.
Update 29.03.2024: Upon a request, the hull as a solid and also the hull splitted into top and bottom halves were uploaded in the STL file format into the Hull_solid_STL folder.

description_text:
Gear pumps are fixed delivery pumps, i.e., they deliver a constant volume at a constant pressure via the meshing of gears.
External Gear Pumps are mostly used for transferring viscous fluids at constant pressure by the rotation of the meshing gears.
External Gear Pumps are also more reliable than centrifugal pumps in terms of transferring viscous fluid under very high pressure. This is because gear pumps use suction by first drawing fluid into the cavity occupied by  the meshing gears and with their rotation push the fluid via the exit hole.

description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 13 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 This is a landing craft I designes because I wanted to experiment with the thrust physic. It does fly, however the thrust needs increasing for use in 1G gravity, as the environment at the moment is only set to 0.3 I think. It can fly upwards, forwards and backwards (however is out of balance in revers.) Please be aware that if you use this craft with any loads, unless perfectly balanced, the craft will tilt and not fly right. It took me a long wile of trial and error to get the thrust distribution perfect, so if you make any changes at all, you will need to move them until they are balanced at all. Wile flying forwards, use the leg extensions as wing. Will in forward flight, push them down to pitch down and up to pitch up (there weigh causes a diffrence in the balance.) Also, wile flying and taking off, make sure the legs are set to 0.5 on the slider, or again, the balance will be off. It is a very sensitive craft. Please rate and review, and feel free to get in touch with me: theexpertdude@gmail.com Skype: the-josh-man

description_text:
A spacecraft is a vehicle, or machine designed to fly in outer space. Spacecraft are used for a variety of purposes, including communications, earth observation, meteorology, navigation, space colonization, planetary exploration, and transportation of humans and cargo.
On a sub-orbital spaceflight, a spacecraft enters space and then returns to the surface, without having gone into an orbit. For orbital spaceflights, spacecraft enter closed orbits around the Earth or around other celestial bodies. Spacecraft used for human spaceflight carry people on board as crew or passengers from start or on orbit (space stations) only, whereas those used for robotic space missions operate either autonomously or telerobotically. Robotic spacecraft used to support scientific research are space probes. Robotic spacecraft that remain in orbit around a planetary body are artificial satellites. Only a handful of interstellar probes, such as Pioneer 10 and 11, Voyager 1 and 2, and New Horizons, are currently on trajectories that leave the Solar System.

description_text:
Smile Extreme Gear – CGI-Style Fan Recreation (Sonic Riders Zero Gravity Inspired)
This is a high-quality, fully custom-made CGI recreation of the Smile Extreme Gear inspired by Sonic Riders: Zero Gravity. Unlike other gears from the series, Smile never received an official CGI appearance in any cutscenes or promotional renders. This model was created as a passion project to imagine how Smile would look if it had appeared in the same cinematic CGI style used in the game’s pre-rendered scenes and marketing artwork.
The goal of this project was to bridge the gap between in-game design and cinematic presentation — keeping the original shape and identity intact while elevating the surface quality, proportions, and materials to match a high-end CGI aesthetic.
Project Goal
In Sonic Riders: Zero Gravity, many Extreme Gears have both in-game and CGI versions, with the CGI ones featuring:
Smoother topology
More refined curves
Physically believable materials
Subtle panel separation and lighting response
However, Smile never received this treatment.This model is a fully imagined CGI adaptation, designed to blend seamlessly with other cinematic Extreme Gear recreations.
It’s not a rip or upscale — everything here was built from scratch to respect the original design while enhancing realism and visual fidelity.
Modeling Approach
The entire model was hand-crafted from the ground up, using the in-game Smile as a visual reference while reinterpreting the geometry to fit CGI standards.
Key Modeling Decisions:
Rebuilt topology to support smooth shading and cinematic renders
Refined curves and proportions for a more believable physical form
Clean panel separations to simulate real manufactured parts
Stylized but believable industrial design language
Extra attention was given to:
Seam flow and curvature continuity
Surface tension and smoothing transitions
Subtle asymmetry where needed to avoid a “toy-like” feel
CGI Style Philosophy
Since Smile never had an official CGI appearance, this version was designed to feel authentic to the Zero Gravity CGI universe.
The styling follows these principles:
Glossy, stylized plastics common in Sonic CGI renders
Bright but grounded color tones
Slightly exaggerated curvature for a premium animated look
Soft but defined panel lines
The result is something that feels:
Familiar to fans
Believable as an official render
Compatible with other CGI Sonic fan recreations
Materials & Look Development
The materials were built to emulate the iconic Sonic Riders CGI look:
High-gloss coated body plastic
Subtle roughness variation to avoid flat reflections
Clean, saturated color separation
Reflective metallic accents where appropriate
The surface response is optimized for:
Studio lighting setups
HDRI rendering
Turntable presentations
Stylized cinematic shots
Technical Details
Polygons: 204,752
Vertices: 204,802
This makes the model suitable for:
High-resolution renders
Close-up shots
Promotional artwork
Portfolio presentation
The density was intentionally kept high to preserve smooth curvature and maintain a cinematic silhouette without faceting under strong lighting.
Topology
The mesh was designed with:
Clean edge flow
Consistent smoothing behavior
Subdivision-friendly structure (depending on workflow)
While primarily intended for rendering, the model remains organized and readable for artists who want to:
Study the topology
Modify parts
Retexture or re-shade
Accuracy & Interpretation
Because Smile lacks an official CGI counterpart, some creative interpretation was necessary.
This model aims to:
Stay faithful to the original in-game identity
Match the visual language of CGI Extreme Gears
Feel like a natural “what if it existed” version
It should feel authentic enough that it could sit alongside:
CGI Blue Star-style recreations
Other cinematic Extreme Gear fan projects
Stylized Sonic universe renders
Use Cases
You are free to use this model for:
Personal renders
Fan art and animation
Portfolio work
Non-commercial creative projects
Study/reference purposes
It’s especially ideal for:
Sonic fan cinematics
Extreme Gear showcases
Stylized product-style renders
Why It’s Free
This model is released for free as a contribution to the Sonic fan and 3D art community.
The intention is to:
Fill a gap that never existed officially
Give artists a high-quality Smile interpretation
Help creators build better Sonic-themed renders
Share passion for Extreme Gear design
If you find it useful, consider:
Crediting the creator
Sharing your renders
Supporting future projects
Notes
This is a fan-made recreation, not an official SEGA asset.
Built with love and attention to detail by a Sonic fan and 3D artist.
Designed to visually match CGI Extreme Gear aesthetics.
Final Words
Smile has always been one of the more unique Extreme Gears, and bringing it into a CGI-style form was a really fun challenge. Since it never received a cinematic version, this project was an opportunity to explore what it could have been if it had appeared in Zero Gravity’s pre-rendered scenes.

description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 8 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 Here is a single wide modular home (manufactured home). The term manufactured means this was built on a factory's assembly line then trucked to the site. Anyway, about this trailer, it has the standard 3 bedroom 2 bathroom configueration. The master bedroom has its own bath and walk-in closet on the far end of the house. The mobile house has a nice kitchen that also shares with the dining. Yes, like most trailer houses of its kind, it has open kitchen, living, and dining. Behind the kitchen is a hidden laundry room. Sort of like a secret entrance. You'll see once you get inside. So yeah, this home essentially has the trailer feeling. Heck, it even includes the screen door, water heater, central heat, linoleum, mostly carpet, plain doors, cheap metal windows, low vaulted ceilings, skirting, and the stairs. Not all of these homes had tounges (used to pull these houses by truck) so I didn't include a tounge on this one. IDK, I might include one in the future. Though the roof can be removed via the layers toolbar, go inside with the roof on the house. I made this model specifically for you to feel like you are actually in one of these modular homes. I have been inside so many of these, I know exactly how it feels. This one in particular is an older one, note the old looking metal cladding about the exterior. It is perfect in any trailer park setting, you may put it anywhere. So, enjoy your camper, hehe, just kidding :) No, really, enjoy and please rate :)

The capacity of the B-52 makes it the perfect aircraft to act as a carpet bomber.   The B-52 is not capable of penitrating heavily defended airspace, but it can strike targets in by sandoff weapons like cruise missiles.  
Yet eventually there is going to need to be a replacement and ideally an upgrade.   This is my brainstorm of what such an aircraft might look like.   With huge internal bomb bays and pilons it can carry tremendous amounts of weaponry.  Turbofans provide both good preformance and range.  Though not a stealth aircraft, it would incorporate new technologies to improve survivability and reduce detection.
An huge raydome in the nose, providing both terrain -following radar capabilities and a place to mount electronic warfare and observational hardware.   The upper deck houses crew accomidations, for long missions for command personel or intellegence workstations, thus the aircraft can be used in some of the capacities as a EC-135 or other command post aircraft.
Radar controled guns provide some level of defene against missiles or other aircraft, in a capacity similar to the CIWS systems.   These guns along with other attachable gatling guns and cannons can also be turned toward the ground, allowing the aircraft to be configured in a ground-support role, similar to the AC-130.

description_text:
This is an upgraded axle design made to resemble old military axles, rockwell 5 ton axles that were used on 1980's era Monster Trucks.  The files consist of a two piece axle casing, 2 piece hubs, and Suspension mounts for shocks and links and/or leaf springs.  I recently added a bracket to mount the servo behind the axle. To complete these axles you need the following parts.

  - 5mm to 6mm aluminum shaft couplers https://www.ebay.com/itm/Shaft-Coupling-5mm-to-6mm-Bore-L20xD12-Robot-Motor-Wheel-Rigid-Coupler-Red-2-PCS/323735699060?hash=item4b6026be74:g:VJoAAOSwvXReqE79

  - Traxxas Tmaxx 3.3 complete Differentials

  - Kyosho Mad Crusher Hub Carriers (You will cut these to length), Knuckles and bearings, 17mm hubs, dog bones shafts (you will cut these to length), outer axle shafts

  - JConcepts Tribute Wheels.  Designed to bolt wheel directly to printed hub using the 6 hole pattern and M3 screws.

  - Width of axle with wheels installed is approximately the same width as a Tamiya TXT-2 and is adjustable to preference based on how short you cut the Hub Carriers.

description_text:
Low poly and low resolution small remote motel with period vehicles, furniture, and appliances. Poly count was kept low and texture resolution was kept below 128 except the car and truck which is 256 each.
The idea was to create a simple retro console style scene but with a modern renderer and an FPU and I think it looks pretty good (https://pixelfed.social/p/troikaime/246478785023709184).
Some objects are uniquely unwrapped between 0-1 but many are not, I've dropped this scene into about half a dozen game engines and it looks good in all of them though you may need some slight tweaking depending on the import process. If you want absolute performance you should consider packing all unique textures into an atlas as the initial texture load is the most expensive step but I don't think there's a machine out there that would struggle with this scene.
The Unity Package was create for 2020.2 HDRP lit shaders, but works fine with other versions and rendering pipelines after you adjust the shaders.

A Low-poly truck for highways coloured red with tiresA truck or lorry is a motor vehicle designed to transport cargo, carry specialized payloads, or perform other utilitarian work. Trucks vary greatly in size, power, and configuration, but the vast majority feature body-on-frame construction, with a cabin that is independent of the payload portion of the vehicle. Smaller varieties may be mechanically similar to some automobiles. Commercial trucks can be very large and powerful and may be configured to be mounted with specialized equipment, such as in the case of refuse trucks, fire trucks, concrete mixers, and suction excavators. In American English, a commercial vehicle without a trailer or other articulation is formally a straight truck while one designed specifically to pull a trailer is not a truck but a tractor.[1]
The majority of trucks currently in use are still powered by diesel engines, although small- to medium-size trucks with gasoline engines exist in the US, Canada, and Mexico. The market-share of electrically powered trucks is growing rapidly, expected to reach 7% globally by 2027, and electric motive force already predominates among both the largest and smallest trucks.[2] In the European Union, vehicles with a gross combination mass of up to 3.5 t (3.4 long tons; 3.9 short tons) are known as light commercial vehicles, and those over as large goods vehicles.

description_text:
This is a highly-detailed model of a train bogie series 18-100, widely used in USSR/Russian/CIS freight wagons. 
The height from rail level to the top of bogie is 9.5mm when using 10.7mm wheelsets (36" prototypical), e.g.  from aliexpress. Sockets for wheelsets follow NEM 314 (Carriage Wheelset for Tip Bearings. This model does not contain wheelsets! I strongly advise using ready-made metal wheelsets for better rolling performance, but if you really want, you can 3D print the wheelsets too, the wheels can be found here, for example: https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:3117985
Center hole is for 2mm self-tapping screw or M2 metal screw, hole can be drilled out for larger screws.
You will need 2 prints of Bogie (print flat side down), one of each of Beam top (print upside up) and Beam bottom (print upside down). There is also an optional NEM 362 pocket for couplings, Coupler pocket (print upside down).
This is a model with tiny details and requires the finest resolution you can get from your printer. I used 0.12mm layer height, 0.08 will be even better. 
I've used PLA on Ender 3 with stock 0.4 mm nozzle. After printing, I glued everything together with super glue, primed with primer-filler spray and painted with a brush. 
A lot of photos of the original can be viewed on scaletrainsclub.com forum: 

  - https://scaletrainsclub.com/board/viewtopic.php?f=46

  - https://scaletrainsclub.com/board/viewtopic.php?t=3204

description_text:
The RAR file contains:
1.) 3 Blender files:
LONGBOARD - a blender file with the board model (709360 vertices). The model consists of 7 parts: board (1), trucks (2),  wheels(4). There are 24 different looks of the board (6 types of the deck material - light/dark, light/dark with the Ballon, light/dark with the Umbrella Cat) and 4 wheel colors (black, orange, pink, blue). All the textures are packed into the blender file and they also exist separately in a folder in the RAR file. There are 2K and 4K textures available.
LONGBOARD_PROCEDURAL_MATERIALS - a blender file with the board model with procedural material (light deck wood with no image, pink wheels) - you can make your own drawing and adjust the colors as you wish :) 
LONGBOARD_RIGGED - a blender file with the rigged board. The rig allows to move and rotate the board, rotate the trucks, tilt the board, rotate the wheels. You can rotate the board around the center pivot and around the front and back truck. However, there is a rig limitation concerning the rotation around one of the 3 rotation axis (you can see it in the youtube clip).
2.) Baked Texures:LONGBOARD_2K/LONGBOARD_2K - textures for the material setup (BOARD-6 diffuse maps, 1 normal map; TRUCKS- diffuse, metallic, normal, roughness map; WHEELS- 4 diffuse maps, normal and roughness)UV - the folder contains png pictures with a default UV mapping (for wheels, trucks and the deck sparately)
3.) OBJ and FBX file (only model, no materials)
4.) 2 MP4 clips regarding the material setup and the rig (YT clip)

description_text:
The Oliver Hazard Perry class was a class of frigates designed and built by the US Navy as well as other nations. Overall 71 units have been built, serving not only in the US, but also under Turkish, Egyptian, Polish, Pakistani, Taiwanese, Bahrain, Australian, Spanish and Chilean flag. The first few units have entered service in 1977 and only 45 have been retired so far. Where as the US pulled the ships out of service in the mid 2010s, some nations aquired the retired these units and put them into their own service. Other nations built their own ships in license also, being Australia, Spain and Taiwan.
Overall the class is quite small compared to other classes, especially considering that the Spruance, Ticonderoga and other classes were much more heavily armed. However, the main task of the class was to escort larger forces, being built in large numbers. Each unit didnt have to be strong in order to protect much more vital assets. Due to this reason, only one MK13 Missile Launcher on the bow, one 76mm OTO Melara main cannon, two triple Mk32 torpedo launchers as well as a single MK15 Phalanx CIWS were carried. Some nations changed the design a bit, for example adding an 8-cell MK41 VLS in the case of the Australian Adelaide-class. To facilitate larger helicopters, the long-hull ships were built, having gotten a 2m longer stern at the flightdeck. The remaining short-hull ships were built like intended, with a slightly smaller displacement.
Despite being a class not designed for large operations and heavy lifting, several nations still prefer using them in regular duty. Taiwan modernized and altered the ships enough to keep them up to date with many foreign threats, Australia retired their frigates only a few years ago, they are now in service in Chile. Spain is also still using their ships, joining the Polish as being the only european nation still doing so. A design not built and intended to last long against any large soviet ship turned out to be a well liked choice of warship which lasts many years. It is expected that some ships of the class will serve until late in the 2020s.
The USS McClusky was laid down in 1981 and entered service in 1983. From the commissioning on, the ship was sent onto several patrols and exercises, spanning up to her decommissioning. Some noteworthy happenings include guarding USS Enterprise, in the Indian Ocean in 1986. In 1988 she took part in an exercise in the middle East, followed by another deployment in 1990 where she would visit Kuwait. Also in 1990, she hosted the visit of three soviet ships in San Diego. As 1991 closed in her homeport was shifted to Yokosuka in Japan, where she would assist in evactuating civillians from the philippines after a vulcano broke out. During her carrer she was awarded the Battle E several times, the last one was awarded in 2013. After a lenghty carreer, it was decided to sell her and USS Curts to the Mexican Navy, that deal failed shortly after. She was decommissioned in 2015 after 31 years of service, being sent into reserve fleet. It was decided to sink her in the RIMPAC 2018 exercise, where she was ultimately sunk 55 nautical miles off Hawaii on the 19th of July.
Note: This model is recommended to be used in the 1/3000 scale. The models itself isnt scaled, the scale table is down below.
1/4000: 3,45cm or 1,35in
1/3000: 4,6cm or 1,81in
1/2000: 6,9cm or 2,71in
1/1000: 13,8cm or 5,43in
For self calculation: The USS McClusky was roughly 138m or 453ft long.
The model is intended to be used with little supports as possible, yet some are recommended below the barrel of the main gun and the main masts. Be carefull when removing the support structures, as the guns and launcher are quite fragile. I recommend using a resin printer for this. Up and Downsclaling might be possible, yet I dont know to what extend.

description_text:
Low poly stylized battle tank, very light and ideal for game developement. Included are the blend file, fbx and obj models. The model is already UV unwrapped and there are various maps available in both 2048x2048px  and 4096x4096px resolution:

  - Diffuse, 2 different skins available

  - Roughness, 2 different roughness maps available

  - Metalness

  - Ambient Occlusion

  - Normals

This way you your model is ready to be used and you have full control over it if you want to customize it. In the blend file there is also the full node based procedural material setup. All maps and objects are neatly named and ordered. The tracks are fully movable and can roll thanks to a curve modifier, just select in the blend file the tracks object and move it back and forth. The tank is UV unwrapped in 3 main parts:

  - The body that consists in the main body of the tank, the armor plates on the side and the turret and cannon. 

  - The tracks and wheels.

  - The extras that are all the secondary objects such as the machine gun on the turret, antenna module, launcher on the back of the turrent, lights and door.

The .blend file does not contain the lighting setup and scene used for rendering, you get the clean tank model as shown in the thumbnail.
If you have problems or need different formats don't hesitate to contact me and I'll do my best to help you.

description_text:
I made this truck by combining parts of scanned modes and then baking both texture and geometry data onto a low poly mesh. Most of the process was done using Blender with minor texture changes done in Substance Painter.
I used the folllowing models:
Toyota Pickup truck by alban CC-BY
Chevy Impala Undercarriage by omegadarling CC-BY
Moldering Minivan (Free Raw Scan) by Renafox CC-BY
It’s pretty interesting workflow that allows to quickly make fairly photorealistic models of objects that wouldn’t be easy to find and scan in real life.Like this technical. Improvised military vehicle created by cutting off the roof of pickup truck and mounting in a machine gun in a cargo bed. Cars like this saw use in the Chadian–Libyan conflict that thanks to the wide use of converted Hiluxes and Land Cruisers was called “Toyota War’‘.

description_text:
This is my first mini transformable transformer.  It is a flexible, articulated robot, able to turn into a truck.  The model is simple to build, no glue is required and all pieces fit together securely.  Out of all the components, only three require support.  While the rest are ready directly from the print bed.  The pieces are colour separated, to allow for full customization.  
In truck mode, the design is clean, minimalist, and robust. It is slammed to the ground for a stealthy appearance.  
Once transformed into its robot form, it has a solid and mechanical look.  It is fully articulated, which allows for a wide range of movements.  The legs are designed with front, back and side movements.  The hips can be rotated, and its arms can swing back and forth.  Its fists can extend to look more aggressive.  
*The Assembly Manual is here. It includes images. https://docs.google.com/document/d/1fGekea9jmyO6yifXGUxlnZnA4XHyAfBiyc8kCLD2xTA/edit?tab=t.0 before printing.  *
On the website cults,  There are better gifs to show the robot.  It's unfortunate, I can't upload gifs on this site.  Search Articulated Robot-Model 1, and you will find it.  This site also don't allow me to put in links.  
Print setting:I used the creality black PLA filament and printed it with the Flsun V400.  
The prints are best fitted with these settings:Layer height: 0.3mmLine width:  0.57mmInfill:  30%Ironing: onSupport: normalPut support blocks on all arches.
Increase all component’s size to 150%.  It’s the minimum size required for this model to work.  
The design is for Fdm printing.  I cannot guarantee resin printing would work.  
Please read:This design is copyrighted.
Your purchase gives you the right to download and print the design for personal use.  Do not resell or redistribute those digital files.  If you wish to create an altered version of my design, please message me beforehand.  
*Attention: *Not suitable for unsupervised play by small children or pets.  The small parts can pose a choking hazard.  Not recommended for children under 3.  
Thanks for reading, Enjoy!

description_text:
The legendary PV3S is an all-terrain multi-purpose truck, (produced between 1953 and 1990) originally designed for the Czechoslovak armed forces, was a durable, popular and extremely adaptable truck built in various versions and was widely exported (72 countries). The truck was among the best off-road cargo vehicles of its time with Czechoslovak army using it for more than half a century.
PV3S Truck – Civilian Platform includes 6 mid-to-low-poly LoD levels (LoD0 is very detailed and can optionally be excluded). Uncovered rear frame allows potential installation of any kind of your own flatbed extension, all wheels are removable.
The truck is fully rigged, controlled by animation scripts which allow steering, frame twisting and suspension movement according to the underlaying terrain.
Available as a complete Unity package file set up for Universal Scriptable Rendering Pipeline, PBR specular (model and textures are backward compatible with built-in RP or convertible into HDRP).

12 PV3S Truck textures (4096 x 4096 pixels)

  - Albedo (specular workflow)

  - Smoothness

  - Specular

  - Normal

4 PV3S Truck meshes (UV mapped) in FBX format (at LoD0)

  - PV3S Truck (319 692 triangles)

  - PV3S Wheel (40 170 triangles)

5 URP PBR (specular) materials
2 PV3S Truck prefabs
7 Audio tracks
1 preview scene with related utility files

description_text:
The Willys MB (pronounced / ˈ w ɪ l ɪ s /, Willis) and the Ford GPW, both formally called the U.S. Army truck, 1⁄4‑ton, 4×4, command reconnaissance, commonly known as the Willys Jeep, Jeep, or jeep, and sometimes referred to by its Standard Army vehicle supply number G-503, were highly successful American off-road capable, light military utility vehicles. Well over 600,000 were built to a single standardized design, for the United States and the Allied forces in World War II, from 1941 until 1945. This also made it (by its light weight) the world's first mass-produced four-wheel-drive car, built in six-figure numbers.
The 1⁄4-ton jeep became the primary light, wheeled, multi-role vehicle of the United States military and its allies. With some 640,000 units built, the 1⁄4‑ton jeeps constituted a quarter of the total military support motor vehicles that the U.S. produced during the war, and almost two-thirds of the 988,000 light 4WD vehicles produced, when counted together with the Dodge WC series. Large numbers of jeeps were provided to U.S. allies, including the Soviet Union at the time. Aside from large amounts of 11⁄2- and 21⁄2‑ton trucks, and 25,000 3⁄4‑ton Dodges, some 50,000 1⁄4‑ton jeeps were shipped to help Russia during WWII, against Nazi Germany's total production of just over 50,000 Kübelwagens, the jeep's primary counterpart.
Historian Charles K. Hyde wrote: In many respects, the jeep became the iconic vehicle of World War II, with an almost mythological reputation of toughness, durability, and versatility. It became the workhorse of the American military, replacing horses, other draft animals, and motorcycles in every role, from messaging and cavalry units to supply trains. In addition, improvised field modifications made the jeep capable of just about any other function soldiers could think of.

description_text:
This project was created as an experiment to combine aggressive supercar proportions with a softer and more emotional atmosphere. The goal was to design something futuristic and sharp, while still feeling elegant, clean, and instantly recognizable. Instead of relying on excessive vents and complicated surfaces, the design focuses on controlled lines, balanced proportions, and strong visual identity.
The concept was inspired by retro-futuristic Italian cars, custom hot rods, stealth aircraft, women body shapes, black cats, tulips, and even Turkish tea glass proportions. All of these influences were blended together to create a machine that feels both dangerous and beautiful at the same time.
One of the main identity elements is the unusual rear section, which mixes a pickup-inspired layout with a lounge-like atmosphere rather than a traditional trunk design. The wheel design was also developed as a major visual feature, almost like mechanical jewelry or gothic architecture, helping give the car a sculptural and planted appearance.
This project was modeled and rendered by Fatih Mehmet Yelkenci aka Yelkencidesign as an independent experimental concept. Feel free to use the model as a blank canvas for your own ideas, renders, animations, or custom versions. Credit to Yelkencidesign as the original designer is always appreciated.
